owner: THERM-01 - Future Thermal Analysis capability (method authority for this one method only)
governance_note: The ONE THERM-01-owned governed artifact of the first THERM-01 user slice, under the accepted STAGE27_THERM01_CONDUCTION_TEMPERATURE_DIFFERENCE_METHOD_CONTRACT.md. It carries the method authority (identity, version, model, executed form and derivation), the applicability declarations, the numeric domain, the high-risk screen, the limitations, the fixed disclosure meaning and the source and source-use records. It is NOT a Domain Pack and NOT an entry in domains/domain_provenance.json, and it is never loaded by, and never loads, the CAP-13 artifact. Calculation execution belongs to the shared deterministic calculation and units owner; nothing here is evidence, a specification, a temperature, rating, margin, safety or suitability statement, or a readiness, progression or validation input.

method.model: ONE declared heat path in steady state, with uniform one-dimensional heat flow through ONE constant area, carrying the inventor's own steady heat flow P through the inventor's own total thermal resistance R_theta of exactly that path.
method.executed_form: delta_T = P * R_theta. One multiplication of the two typed inputs; no subtraction, no tolerance, no rounding, no clamping and no magnitude ceiling.
method.derivation: The DOE authority THERM-S1 is the per-area steady-state relation delta_T = q'' * R'' only. The total form is InventorAI's own bounded derivation, valid only under declarations D-1 to D-6: Qdot = q'' * A and R_theta = R'' / A, therefore delta_T = q'' * R'' = (Qdot / A) * R'' = Qdot * (R'' / A) = Qdot * R_theta, with P taken as Qdot. The area, the flux and the per-area resistance are never inputs, outputs or stored values, and no area normalization is performed.

roles.meaning: steady heat flow through the declared path
inventor-supplied total thermal resistance of exactly the declared path (the role written R-theta)
temperature difference across the declared path (the role written Delta-T); never an absolute or component temperature

rules: P and R_theta are finite numbers strictly greater than zero; a string, boolean, NaN, infinity, zero, negative value or any other non-finite or non-numeric value is INVALID_NUMERIC_INPUT, resolved before the shared owner is called.
No physical magnitude ceiling exists, and none is part of the admitted engineering domain.
An overflow or a non-finite delta_T from a finite admitted pair is FAILURE / EXECUTION_INTEGRITY_FAILURE with no numerical payload; it is never rewritten as a refusal.

Each typed numeric field is capped at 64 characters for abuse and resource protection only; that bound is NON-PHYSICAL, is NOT the admitted engineering domain and is never described as a range of valid heat flows or resistances. Over-length text is INVALID_NUMERIC_INPUT.
Grammar: strict ASCII decimal digits with an optional single fractional part; no sign, exponent, separator, Unicode digit, unit suffix or normalization.

declarations.accepted_value: steady state: P is constant and temperatures along the path are no longer changing
ONE path: all of P flows through this path; no parallel path, side loss or other heat source along it
uniform one-dimensional heat flow: the same heat flow crosses every layer of the path evenly
ONE constant area through the whole path: no spreading, constriction or change of area

R_theta is the inventor's own total thermal resistance of exactly this path (the per-area resistance of its layers divided by that one common area), and already includes every layer, interface and surface film the inventor means to cover; InventorAI does not check it
R_theta does not change with P or with temperature over the condition being considered

screen_items.item: a surface people touch, skin contact or medical use
a heat source other than steady electrical dissipation (combustion, chemical or similar)

limitations: No absolute, ambient, junction, case, surface or component temperature; no Celsius and no offset handling; no rating, limit, margin, pass / fail, safety, acceptability, suitability, compliance or specification statement.

No general admission of datasheet R_theta; no lookup, default or inference of R_theta; no material-property, conductivity, convection-coefficient or emissivity data; no convection or radiation modelling, transient analysis, thermal network, parallel paths, spreading resistance, geometry, CFD, FEA or numerical solver.
All NO answers on the high-risk screen only allow this bounded calculation to proceed; they never mean safe. The screen neither reads nor feeds SafetySignal.
The result is UNVALIDATED and is not evidence; it is request-local and is not stored, reported, exported or used for readiness, progression or validation.
disclosure: This is the temperature difference across the one path you declared, under the declared steady-state, single-path, uniform one-dimensional and constant-area conditions, using your own P and Rθ.
It is not a component, junction, case, surface or ambient temperature, and it does not tell what temperature anything reaches.
It is not compared with any rating, limit or margin, and it says nothing about whether anything is safe, acceptable, suitable, compliant or reliable.
It is preliminary, advisory, UNVALIDATED and not evidence, and it must be confirmed by measurement or a thermal specialist before any reliance.
InventorAI does not check Rθ or that your declarations match the real hardware, and a datasheet figure applies only where the real path matches the conditions it was defined under.
Convection, radiation, spreading, transient behaviour and every other path are outside this calculation.
Reference source material: U.S. DOE Fundamentals Handbook (archived; historical fundamentals reference only); the total-resistance form is InventorAI's own derivation.
